Copied Arbitrum escrow gateways: post-fork withdrawal receipt
census
Research date: 29 September 2026. This study audits actual returned gateway withdrawal events and
their successful transaction receipts. It does not create transactions or simulate changes to contract
state.
Scope and findings
The selected range is PulseChain block 17,233,000 through 27,659,393, with endpoint hash 
0xc5e582cd902f4bff3b1aa325b9b564fcd5d6dc0ffa77a03fcd105b65c6390275. Four gateways returned 102
WithdrawalFinalized events across 74 transactions, involving 90 distinct token addresses.
Every event was reconciled to its successful receipt and matching block header. The RPC reported no
query errors.
Gateway Address Returned withdrawal events
Standard 0xa3a7b6f88361f48403514059f1f16c8e7
8d60eec
93
Custom 0xcee284f754e854890e311e3280b767f80
797180d
6
DAI 0xd3b5b60020504bc3489d6949d54589398
2ba3011
2
wstETH 0x0f25c1dc2a9922304f2eac71dca9b07e3
10e8e5a
1
The complete receipts contain no standard ERC-20 Transfer event from the zero address. For 101
withdrawals, the same-token receipt has an exact transfer matching the gateway's amount and
recipient. Their senders are the standard or custom gateway, designated DAI escrow, or wstETH
gateway, as applicable. The remaining withdrawal has two outgoing token transfers whose sum exactly
matches the gateway amount, as described below.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 79

This is a receipt-level screen, not a universal proof that every token's supply was unchanged. T okens
may use nonstandard issuance events, rebasing or modified implementations. Historical traces and
token-specific state reconciliation are needed to classify a positive issuance candidate conclusively.
Endpoint source alone cannot establish what a proxy executed at every historical block.
A token can have withdrawals through more than one gateway
The GRT specialized-gateway mint does not make every GRT withdrawal a mint. The standard gateway
also emitted a GRT withdrawal on 10 November 2024, block 21,896,488, for 
642,162.424364481063167735 GRT, paid to 0x42543853a72edb6f1ff9bddab0cf4676187ec28a. Its matching
Transfer comes from the standard gateway, and its receipt contains no zero-address Transfer. Recorded
GRT standard-gateway transaction.
The custom gateway also emitted an LPT withdrawal for 2 LPT, paid to 
0xa0b347117a878da9942fa5c31b87c773a2969913, on 1 September 2026, block 27,434,939. The matching
transfer comes from that custom gateway. The transaction contains two selected withdrawal events; the
other token's event is counted separately in the census. Recorded LPT custom-gateway transaction.
These observations are why an audit should search gateway execution history, not only the router's
current preferred mapping for each token. They do not establish that those transactions share a human
controller or that one financed the other.
Split-transfer reconciliation
At token 0x45804880de22913dafe09f4980848ece6ecbaf78, the recorded gateway amount is 
10,333,968,436,222,304,303 raw units. The receipt contains two transfers from the standard
gateway: one to the withdrawal recipient and one to 0x38699d04656ff537ef8671b6b595402ebdbdf6f4. Their raw
amounts sum exactly to the gateway amount. Therefore the recipient-only exact-amount check fails,
while the gross transfer reconciliation succeeds. This study does not infer new issuance from that
difference or independently establish the second recipient's purpose. Split-transfer receipt.
Historical gateway discovery
Re-reading all 167 saved router registration logs identifies one additional historical gateway beyond the
nine effective gateway addresses in the endpoint inventory: retired LPT gateway 
0xd82c27966ebb293b2d8646d8eacb293bc260698e. Its registration predates the fork. The explorer identifies verified 
L1LPTGateway source. Zero-address default routing and the address-one disabled sentinel are not counted
as gateways. The separate specialized-gateway study checks this historical address too.
This yields ten identified gateway addresses across the returned registration history,
compared with nine effective endpoint addresses. Combining this study with the specialized-gateway
history (Appendix 20) and GRT withdrawal history (Appendix 12) yields 106 returned withdrawal
events in 78 distinct transactions, involving 91 token addresses across those ten gateways. It
remains bounded to this router and the available logs, not every bridge deployment on PulseChain.
Method and reproduction
The new explicit manifest is Research/experiments/parb_escrow_gateway_withdrawals_20260929.json. Run Research/
scripts/collect_pulsechain_events.py --manifest with that file and a fresh --output path. The collector verifies
chain 369, the endpoint header, successful receipts and inclusion of each returned event.
The event signature is WithdrawalFinalized(address,address,address,uint256,uint256), verified in each
gateway's retained source/interface. T oken identity and amount are decoded from the event data;
recipient is decoded from its indexed topic. The receipt screen compares each event against same-token
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 80

Transfer logs and separately checks all receipt Transfer logs for a zero sender. A mint event in the same
receipt would be a candidate, not proof of a causal gateway mint: the trace would still need to connect
the gateway call to token issuance.
Raw records, decoded receipt screening, historical-gateway source/registration and SHA-256 hashes are
retained under ignored artifacts/parb-escrow-gateway-withdrawals-20260929/. The earlier source and router
inventory remain frozen in their original batch. Provider history completeness, unqueried event
signatures and other routers remain limitations. No production code changed; production tests are not
applicable to this study.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 81
